units.translation: With this accent in both places M. The opinion of certain grammarians was that the adjectives πονηρος [wicked] and μοχθηρος [wretched], when they have the meaning of bad or wicked, were pronounced by the Attics with an acute accent on the last syllable, but when they mean laborious or afflicted, with an acute accent on the antepenult; this is reported by Herodian in Arcadius p. 71, 16 and Ammonius p. 95. More correctly Trypho, who alone approved the accentuation μοχθηρός [wretched], with no distinction of meaning, as Ammonius reports p. 116, with whom Eustathius p. 341, 14 agrees, that all other adjectives of this kind, such as καματηρός [toilsome] and ὀλισθηρός [slippery], are oxytone.
ETEOCLES: O Zeus, what a race of women you have granted! CHORUS: A wretched one, just like men whose city is captured.
And many wretched and unprofitable things will you endure for me.
